items.text: Every episode loses most of its audience right at the start: E1 opens with 67.3 of 100 watching but only 11.7 remain at the 2% mark; E3 opens at 73 and falls to 12.1. In E1, 8 of every 100 viewers left around minute 7 during in-progress housekeeping talk.
items.recommendation: Test a tighter cold open this week: lead with the single strongest demo or story in the first minute, move housekeeping and show-status chatter to after the rebound peak, and compare the 2% mark next episode.

items.text: E1 converted 8.9 subscribers per 1,000 views (13.3 on DesignerTom), but E3 converted 0 on both channels and E5 just 0.9. Whatever E1 did to turn viewers into subscribers has disappeared.
items.recommendation: Rewatch E1 and copy its subscribe moments. Script two clear asks per show — one near the early rebound peak, one mid-show — each tied to a concrete reason to subscribe, and check per-episode conversion next week.

items.text: DesignerTom gained 0 subscribers in E3, E4, E5 and E6, and sits at 2.2 per 1,000 views overall versus Dive Club's 3.4. Its share watched is also lower: 9.7 versus 11.1.
items.recommendation: Treat DesignerTom as its own audience this week: pin a comment with a reason to subscribe, test a title and thumbnail written for Tom's followers rather than reusing the Dive Club framing, and compare subscribers gained on the next episode.

items.text: 54.7 of every 100 YouTube views come from existing subscribers. Discovery surfaces are near zero: Shorts brought 2 views, end screens 7, playlists 56.
items.recommendation: This week, cut three Shorts from the best E5 moments, add end screens on every past episode pointing to the newest one, and publish a single show playlist. Any lift from these surfaces is nearly free reach.

items.text: E5 held viewers best: 17.6 of 100 through the middle half and 11.7 near the end. A bit past halfway, around minute 53, showing the week's HTML prototypes lined up with 2.8 extra viewers of every 100 watching.
items.recommendation: Structure next episode around scheduled screen-share demos — one every segment — and tease the biggest one in the opening. Test whether the middle half holds above E5's level.

items.text: Peak live viewers fell from 90 in E1 to 53 in E3, recovering only to 71 by E6. Chat fell harder: 383 messages in E1 down to 100 in E5 and 127 in E6.
items.recommendation: Lock a consistent day and time, announce the agenda on both channels and X a day ahead, and bring back an interactive segment like designer of the week with a call for chat nominations. Compare peak viewers and chat volume over the next two shows.
